text.tspan: ADR
ADR-002
Strict JSJSON Canonical Storage — Decision: Aurora cards are stored
as strict JSON using the .jsjson extension. Rationale: deterministic
diffs, wide tool compatibility, and unambiguous machine parsing.
Trade-off: no comments; humans must rely on explicit fields and Notes
instead.
Capability
CAP-015
Deterministic Model Invariants — Ability to define and enforce
mission-rooted graph invariants so any tool can traverse, validate, and
interpret the model deterministically.
Capability
CAP-016
Canonical Registries — Ability to define and distribute canonical
registries for card types, relationship verbs, and views so multiple
tools produce consistent validation and renderings.
Capability
CAP-017
Model Layout and Serialization — Ability to persist Aurora cards in
a stable, tooling-friendly directory and filename layout, with schema
references and encoding rules suitable for reliable diffs and
automated ingestion.
Capability
CAP-018
View Projection and Rendering — Ability to select card types for a
view and render the resulting subgraph as navigable documentation and
diagrams without altering the underlying model.
Driver
DRI-006
Deterministic Architectural Language — Enable unambiguous
interpretation and automated reasoning by enforcing deterministic model
structure and traversal rules rooted at the Mission card.
Driver
DRI-007
Machine and Human Readable Source of Truth — Ensure Aurora models
remain directly interpretable by expert practitioners while staying
friendly to machine parsing, tooling, and agent consumption.
Driver
DRI-008
Canonical Registries and View Definitions — Provide a stable, shared
vocabulary for cards, relationship verbs, and views so validation and
rendering can be deterministic and portable across tools.
Mission
MIS-001
Agent-Unified Representation of Requirements and Architecture (Aurora)
— A rigorous, MBSE-class architectural modeling framework designed for
equal readability by human engineers, machine learning ("AI") agents,
and computer programs. It provides a lightweight but complete
representational schema that captures requirements, behavior, structure,
interfaces, constraints, and traceability in a single, coherent model.
The objective is a common architectural language that supports automated
reasoning, validation, and lifecycle tooling while remaining directly
interpretable by expert practitioners. Because it is designed to be
readable by machine agents as well as humans, Aurora artifacts can be
generated by machine learning models, consumed by coding agents, and
used to automatically generate views of the architecture.
Requirement
REQ-016
Strict JSJSON Card Encoding — Aurora card files SHALL be stored as
strict JSON (RFC 8259) using the .jsjson extension: double quotes, no
comments, no trailing commas, UTF-8 encoding, and exactly one
trailing newline.
Requirement
REQ-017
Identifiers, Filenames, and Model Layout — Aurora cards SHALL use
stable identifiers (e.g., MIS-001) that MUST NOT change once issued.
Card files SHALL be named <id>-<Sanitized_Name>.jsjson, where special
characters are stripped and spaces are replaced with underscores. Models
SHALL follow the Model Home and Mission folder layout conventions so
tools can discover, validate, and render deterministically.
Requirement
REQ-018
Single Root Mission — Each Aurora model SHALL start with exactly one
Mission card that serves as the root of the directed graph. The Mission
card SHALL only have outgoing links and SHALL provide a consistent
starting point for traversal and view generation.
Requirement
REQ-019
Directed Graph with Local Cycles — All Aurora links SHALL lead away
from the Mission card. Local cycles MAY exist within bounded subgraphs
(for example state machines) as long as no link creates a path back to
the Mission.
Requirement
REQ-020
Boundary and Note Semantics — Boundary cards SHALL be used to group
related cards for rendering and navigation; they may have a subtype such
as End to limit recursion. Note cards SHALL be used only as annotative
leaves (incoming links only) and SHALL NOT introduce new structural
model elements.
Requirement
REQ-021
Canonical Card Registry — Aurora tooling and documentation SHALL use
a canonical registry of card types (and optional subtypes) to support
consistent rendering, validation, and communication across tools.
Requirement
REQ-022
Canonical Relationship Registry — Aurora tooling and documentation
SHALL use a canonical registry of relationship verbs, including
allowed source and target card types, to enable deterministic
validation and interoperable views.
Requirement
REQ-023
Canonical View Registry — Aurora tooling and documentation SHALL
use a canonical registry of view definitions that declare which card
types are included and what root types anchor each view.
Requirement
REQ-024
Schema Referencing Rules — All Aurora card files SHALL include a
$schema field referencing the applicable Aurora schema using a relative
path from the card file to the Model Home schema file.
Requirement
REQ-025
Model Integrity Validation — Aurora models SHALL be
machine-validatable for integrity: every non-Mission, non-Note card
SHALL have at least one incoming link; every card SHALL be reachable
from the Mission; and all links[].target values SHALL reference an
existing card id.
Requirement
REQ-026
Views as Projections — Views SHALL be treated as projections of a
single underlying model graph by selecting a set of card types (and
optional subtypes) and rendering only those cards and the links
between them; views SHALL NOT change the underlying model.
Requirement
REQ-027
Audit Trail and Versioning — All Aurora cards SHALL include an
audit_trail with a per-card SemVer version, an optional SHA256 hash
(nullable), and a chronological history of created/edited/deleted
events including editor identity and RFC3339 timestamps.
Requirement
REQ-028
Semantics Derived from Invariants — Aurora card and relationship
labels SHALL be treated as descriptive metadata; the meaning of the
architecture SHALL be derived from the model’s invariant rules and
the current view’s inclusion/projection of card types and links.
